item.title: Heterogeneous Electric Double Layer with Ion‐Transport Pathways for Practical Zinc‐Ion Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This work pioneers heterogeneous EDL nanostructure engineering via cation-anion coordination, creating ion-transport pathways that stabilize Zn anodes. It achieves record Zn²⁺ transference (0.89), 30,000-cycle full-cell stability, and practical Ah-level pouch cells, offering a new paradigm for durable aqueous zinc-ion batteries.

item.title: Built‐In Electric Fields in Rechargeable Batteries: Formation Mechanisms, Functional Roles, and Design Principles
item.description:

Advanced Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This review uniquely systematizes built-in electric fields (BIEFs) in rechargeable batteries, covering formation mechanisms, characterization, theoretical calculations, and roles in anodes, cathodes, and electrolytes. It bridges knowledge gaps by linking BIEF engineering strategies to design principles, offering actionable guidance for suppressing instability and enhancing kinetics in next-generation high-energy, long-life batteries.

item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 This study identifies a new low-temperature interfacial relaxation process in Al anodes via in situ EIS-DRT, revealing that impedance surge arises from a disordered Al₂O₃-rich layer, not reduced electrolyte conductivity. This mechanistic insight challenges conventional assumptions and provides a basis for interfacial engineering of low-temperature-adaptable aqueous Al batteries.

item.title: Host–Guest Engineering for Advanced Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This Review uniquely frames host–guest engineering as a molecular-level strategy to control transient ionic and reactive states across electrolytes, interfaces, and conversion cathodes. Its cross-scenario quantitative comparison reveals that optimal battery performance requires balancing guest-regulation effectiveness with dynamic flexibility, not maximal binding. It thereby unifies disparate battery chemistries and guides future adaptive host design.

💡 The novelty lies in using Ni/NiO heterointerfaces to create a built-in electric field that redistributes charge and promotes a LiF-rich SEI. It offers a promising interface-engineering strategy for high-energy-density anode design.
